description_full: Global-E Online Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, provides direct-to-consumer cross-border e-commerce platform in Israel, the United Kingdom, the United States, and internationally. Its platform enables international shoppers to buy online, and merchants to sell from and to worldwide. The company was incorporated in 2013 and is headquartered in Petah Tikva, Israel.
ceo_bio: Mr. Amir  Schlachet | Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman of the Board | Age 48 | Compensation: $714,000 (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $789K ranks in the top quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, improving at 41%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $230K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $32K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: Global-E Online Ltd. is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $7.2B market cap on $962M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +33% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +8.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -19% against a 12% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 41%.

The business throws off $281M in free cash flow — roughly 29 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -14.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 30% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
